item.title: Florida DBPR wraps enforcement push against unlicensed contractors
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation completed a two-week statewide crackdown on unlicensed contractors last month, with enforcement teams operating from offices across the state including Pensacola. From October 12 through 23, the initiative — conducted in partnership with the National Association of State Contractors…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation completed a two-week statewide crackdown on unlicensed contractors last month, with enforcement teams operating from offices across the state including Pensacola. From October 12 through 23, the initiative — conducted in partnership with the National Association of State Contractors Licensing Agencies — conducted over 1,300 license checks and visited nearly 2,000 sites to identify violations.

DBPR Secretary Melanie Griffin said the effort underscores the agency's commitment to protecting consumers and licensed professionals. "Unlicensed contracting puts Floridians' safety and hard-earned money at risk and undercuts the licensed professionals who follow the law," she said in a statement. The operation identified 55 cases of suspected unlicensed activity and included a sting operation alongside compliance sweeps and outreach activities.

Beyond enforcement, regional teams conducted 61 outreach activities statewide to educate consumers about the importance of verifying a contractor's license before hiring. DBPR encourages Floridians to check licenses at MyFloridaLicense.com or call the Unlicensed Activity Hotline at (866) 532-1440 to report suspected violations. The agency also operates HireSmartFL.com and RebuildRightFL.com as consumer resources for finding licensed professionals, particularly for post-storm repairs.

item.title: UWF to premiere Vietnam veteran oral history documentary Nov. 10
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The University of West Florida will premiere a documentary capturing the stories of Vietnam veterans living in Pensacola, drawing on a yearlong oral history project that gave students hands-on training in historical research and preservation. "Their Vietnam: Voices of Azalea Trace" will screen Tuesday, Nov. 10, at the UWF Center for Fine and…
item.content:encoded:
The University of West Florida will premiere a documentary capturing the stories of Vietnam veterans living in Pensacola, drawing on a yearlong oral history project that gave students hands-on training in historical research and preservation.

"Their Vietnam: Voices of Azalea Trace" will screen Tuesday, Nov. 10, at the UWF Center for Fine and Performing Arts Mainstage Theatre. A public reception begins at 6:30 p.m., with the film starting at 7 p.m. The event is free and open to the public, though registration is requested through UWF's website.

The roughly 1-hour-40-minute documentary grew out of interviews conducted by UWF undergraduate and graduate students with residents at Azalea Trace retirement community between September and October 2025. Under the direction of faculty members Joyce Southard and Nathan Smith, students learned transcription, interviewing and archival techniques while recording firsthand accounts of military service. The project aimed to preserve personal histories that might otherwise be lost while giving students practical experience as historians.

Among those featured is Vietnam veteran Miles Davis, who emphasized the importance of recording these accounts while veterans are still able to share them. Rather than presenting a single narrative of the war, the documentary preserves individual perspectives on service, identity and the realities of combat. The oral histories will be archived at UWF for future research and study.

item.title: Baptist Health Care CEO Faulkner to retire June 2027; COO Aldridge named successor
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Mark Faulkner, who has led Baptist Health Care as President and CEO for 14 years, announced Monday that he will step down on June 30, 2027, after 34 years with the Pensacola-based health system. The organization's Board of Directors has named Brett Aldridge, the current Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer, as Faulkner's successor…
item.content:encoded:
Mark Faulkner, who has led Baptist Health Care as President and CEO for 14 years, announced Monday that he will step down on June 30, 2027, after 34 years with the Pensacola-based health system. The organization's Board of Directors has named Brett Aldridge, the current Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer, as Faulkner's successor effective July 1.

Faulkner's tenure has guided Baptist through substantial growth and modernization, including the recent move to a new hospital campus. Under his leadership, Baptist has maintained its position as Northwest Florida's only locally based health care system while expanding services across the region. He also serves on the Florida Hospital Association Board of Trustees and the American Hospital Association Regional Policy Board.

Aldridge, a Pensacola native, joined Baptist in 2010 and has held increasingly senior roles in strategy, operations, and administration. As COO since 2023, he has overseen operational improvements that resulted in top patient satisfaction scores, improved staff retention, record financial results, and the area's only 4-star CMS quality rating. He also led Baptist's pandemic response and the transition to the new hospital campus. Aldridge will be Baptist's fifth CEO in the organization's 75-year history.

item.title: Escambia County property tax collection begins Nov. 1; early payment discounts available
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County Tax Collector Scott Lunsford announced Monday that collection of 2026 property taxes begins November 1, with this year's rolls covering 185,733 accounts totaling more than $545 million. Florida law allows taxpayers to receive discounts for early payment. Payments made in November through December 2 receive a four percent discount,…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County Tax Collector Scott Lunsford announced Monday that collection of 2026 property taxes begins November 1, with this year's rolls covering 185,733 accounts totaling more than $545 million.

Florida law allows taxpayers to receive discounts for early payment. Payments made in November through December 2 receive a four percent discount, three percent in December, two percent in January, and one percent in February. By March 31, 2027, the full amount is due with no discount. Payments made April 1 or later are considered delinquent and subject to penalties.

Taxpayers have multiple payment options, including online at EscambiaTaxCollector.com using eCheck with no extra fees, a 24-hour drop box, or mail. Those struggling with a lump-sum payment can apply for partial payments through March 31 with no discount, or enroll in the Tax Payment Installment Plan to spread payments across four quarterly installments while still receiving early-payment discounts. The installment plan application deadline for 2027 taxes is April 30, 2027.

Tax revenue from this collection supports Escambia County government ($266 million), Escambia County Schools ($200 million), City of Pensacola ($35.6 million), and various special districts including fire protection, stormwater management, and the library system. Taxpayers who don't receive their bill by November 12 can visit the tax collector's website or call 850-438-6500, ext. 3252.

item.title: Warm Monday, then rain Wednesday as cold front moves into NW Florida
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pensacola-area residents can expect mild, breezy conditions to start the week before a significant weather shift midweek, according to the National Weather Service. A strong cold front is expected to push through the region on Wednesday, bringing an 80 percent chance of showers and thunderstorms. Though rain will be widespread, the weather service…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola-area residents can expect mild, breezy conditions to start the week before a significant weather shift midweek, according to the National Weather Service.

A strong cold front is expected to push through the region on Wednesday, bringing an 80 percent chance of showers and thunderstorms. Though rain will be widespread, the weather service says the severe weather threat remains low, so damaging winds or hail are not anticipated.

The cooler air mass behind the front will settle in for the weekend, marking a notable change from today's milder start to November.

item.title: Florida Public Safety Officials Warn Amendment 3 Could Slash Emergency Services
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Public safety leaders across multiple Florida counties are sounding an alarm ahead of Election Day, warning that passage of Amendment 3 could force significant cuts to police and fire services statewide, according to North Escambia reporting. Amendment 3, a major property tax reduction proposal set to appear on Tuesday's ballot, could trigger…
item.content:encoded:
Public safety leaders across multiple Florida counties are sounding an alarm ahead of Election Day, warning that passage of Amendment 3 could force significant cuts to police and fire services statewide, according to North Escambia reporting.

Amendment 3, a major property tax reduction proposal set to appear on Tuesday's ballot, could trigger reduced emergency response times, service cutbacks, and the consolidation of smaller police and fire departments if voters approve it, officials contend. The amendment's funding impact on local governments has become a focal point of debate as Election Day approaches.

Public safety officials have increasingly mobilized to highlight what they view as the operational consequences of the tax cut, arguing that reduced property tax revenue would directly translate to fewer resources for emergency services across Florida communities. The warning reflects broader concerns among municipal and county leaders about how the measure might reshape local government operations.

item.content:encoded:
The University of Florida's Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences (UF/IFAS) Escambia Extension is running its annual Peanut Butter Challenge through Friday, November 20, a friendly food drive competition designed to support regional food pantries.

Coordinated by UF/IFAS Extension and Florida A&M University Cooperative Extension, the challenge invites Escambia County residents and businesses to donate peanut butter and other food items. The campaign is structured as a competition among Florida counties, encouraging communities to contribute generously while supporting neighbors in need.

Donations are being accepted now through November 20. Anyone interested in contributing to help fight local hunger can contact UF/IFAS Escambia Extension for drop-off locations and details on how to participate in the drive.

item.content:encoded:
Thousands of people gathered in downtown Pensacola Saturday morning for the annual Making Strides Against Breast Cancer Walk, an American Cancer Society signature event that drew an estimated 10,000 participants.

The walk brought together community members, many of whom participated to honor loved ones currently battling breast cancer or those they've lost to the disease. The event is one of the nation's largest fundraising walks dedicated to breast cancer awareness and support.

Saturday's turnout underscores the continued community commitment to cancer prevention and support services in the Pensacola area. The walk raises funds for research, education, and patient services through the American Cancer Society.

item.title: FPL proposes lower 2027 rates despite hurricane recovery charge
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The proposal reflects FPL's effort to balance the…
item.content:encoded:
Florida Power & Light has requested a modest rate adjustment for 2027 that would include a specific charge to cover Hurricane Isaias restoration costs, but the overall impact on customer bills would be slightly lower than rates currently approved for this year, according to the utility's filing.

The proposal reflects FPL's effort to balance the costs of ongoing hurricane recovery work with broader rate considerations across its service territory, which includes the Pensacola area and much of North Escambia County. The specific details of how the Hurricane Isaias recovery charge would be structured and what portion of customer bills it would represent have not yet been disclosed.

FPL's rate proposals undergo regulatory review before taking effect. Customers in the region can expect more information as the utility commission evaluates the 2027 rate request in coming weeks.

item.title: FEMA Opens Registration Sites Sunday for Hurricane Isaias Assistance in Escambia County
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County residents affected by Hurricane Isaias can begin registering for federal disaster assistance starting tomorrow. The Federal Emergency Management Agency will operate three registration points throughout the county beginning Sunday, Nov. 1, from 1 p.m. to 5 p.m., then expand hours to 8 a.m.–5 p.m. Monday through Wednesday. The three…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County residents affected by Hurricane Isaias can begin registering for federal disaster assistance starting tomorrow. The Federal Emergency Management Agency will operate three registration points throughout the county beginning Sunday, Nov. 1, from 1 p.m. to 5 p.m., then expand hours to 8 a.m.–5 p.m. Monday through Wednesday.

The three locations are Bayview Senior Center (2000 E. Lloyd St., Pensacola), the Escambia County Central Office Complex (3363 W. Park Place, Pensacola), and Cokesbury Church (5725 N. 9th Ave., Pensacola). State Emergency Response Team staff will be on hand at all sites to walk residents through the FEMA Individual Assistance application process.

Escambia County recently received a FEMA Disaster Declaration for Individual Assistance related to Hurricane Isaias, opening the door to housing assistance, home repair grants, crisis counseling, disaster unemployment benefits, and legal services. Residents can also register online at DisasterAssistance.gov, by calling the FEMA Helpline at 1-800-621-3362 (TTY 1-800-462-7585, available 7 a.m.–10 p.m. daily), or through the FEMA mobile app. For additional details, visit MyEscambia.com or the Escambia County Emergency Management Facebook page.

Details surrounding the investigation and timeline of the alleged bathroom photography remain limited, but the case underscores the severity of allegations facing the former officer across multiple criminal categories.

item.title: Florida Corrections, Local Law Enforcement Checking Sex Offender Compliance This Halloween
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Department of Corrections is conducting its annual Halloween compliance checks on sex offenders under felony supervision throughout the state, including here in the Panhandle, as part of broader community safety efforts during the holiday season. The statewide initiative involves FDC officials and local law enforcement verifying that…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Corrections is conducting its annual Halloween compliance checks on sex offenders under felony supervision throughout the state, including here in the Panhandle, as part of broader community safety efforts during the holiday season.

The statewide initiative involves FDC officials and local law enforcement verifying that supervised sex offenders are following the terms of their release, which typically include restrictions on their movements and activities—particularly around times when children are out in public, like trick-or-treating.

Escambia and Santa Rosa County law enforcement agencies participate in these coordinated checks each October 31st. The compliance verifications help ensure offenders registered with the state are where they're supposed to be and adhering to any court-ordered conditions of their supervision.

Florida's sex offender registry and monitoring program is one of the nation's most stringent. Residents can check the Florida Department of Corrections sex offender database online to learn about registered offenders in their neighborhoods.

item.title: Set Clocks Back Tonight as Daylight Saving Time Ends; Fire Officials Urge Battery Check
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pensacola-area residents should remember to set their clocks back one hour before bed Saturday night as daylight saving time ends and standard time resumes. Fire officials are also using the time change as a reminder for a critical safety step: replace the batteries in your smoke alarms. The seasonal clock change has become a standard public…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola-area residents should remember to set their clocks back one hour before bed Saturday night as daylight saving time ends and standard time resumes.

Fire officials are also using the time change as a reminder for a critical safety step: replace the batteries in your smoke alarms. The seasonal clock change has become a standard public safety reminder for homeowners to check and refresh smoke detector batteries, which can degrade over time and may not function properly in an emergency.

The twice-yearly time changes — "spring forward" in March and "fall back" in October — have long served as convenient calendar markers for routine home maintenance and safety checks. Residents are encouraged not to let the reminder pass by this year.
